authentication.title: OAuth authorization | Get access token - Podio API Documentation
authentication.snippet: Podio supports 4 ways of obtaining an access token: password: Use the end users mail and password to access the API. This is only valid for trusted clients. refresh_token: Use the refresh token obtained previously from one of the above methods. This operation can return a wide variety of error codes. For details see the OAuth 2 specification.

authentication.title: OAuth authorization | API Documentation - Podio
authentication.snippet: To be able to access the API, a third party will have to register with Podio. This will result in a client being created, which can then be used when authenticating.

authentication.title: Authentication - Podio API Documentation
authentication.snippet: The Podio API uses the OAuth2 protocol for authentication. This allows external apps to request authorization to Podio without having direct access to the user's password.

authentication.title: Authentication: Server-side flow - Podio API Documentation
authentication.snippet: The first step is to redirect your user to Podio's authorization endpoint, providing your client_id and a redirect_uri. The redirect_uri must be on the same domain as the domain you specified when you applied for your API Key.

authentication.title: Authentication: Client-side flow - Podio API Documentation
authentication.snippet: Authentication Client-side flow The client-side flow is very similar to the server-side flow. It uses the same concept of redirects, and you should make yourself familiar with the server-side flow first. The only difference between the two is the response_type parameter. For the client-side flow it must be set to "token":

access.snippet: When dealing with people who are Podio users you should always provide their user_id or profile_id rather than an email address. This avoids duplicate user accounts in cases where the person is using a different email than you are anticipating.

webhooks.title: Tutorials: Working with webhooks - Podio API Documentation
webhooks.snippet: Each webhook is registered to receive updates about a specific event in Podio, for example an item being updated or a comment being added. View a full list of supported events in the API reference documentation.

webhooks.title: Webhooks - Podio.com
webhooks.snippet: Webhooks do not have any correlation with any Podio Apps. This means you'll need to either Create a New Item, or Search for an Item in an app using the information posted to the Webhook.

webhooks.title: Developers - Podio API Documentation
